Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

actually adverb

also in fact, in reality, really, as a matter of fact, well … (correcting oneself or another)

classical

Cic. Off. 3.75: quī rē vērā nōn esset hērēs
Cic. Quinct. 56; Fam. 3.5.1 (Lewis & Short)
M-O s.v. really: rē vērā, rēapse

rē vērā (rēvērā)

adverbial ablative

actually, in fact, in reality

The fact set against words or appearances. Rē alone does the same against verbō: “in word … in fact”.

Other words

  • immō — actually (correcting what was said): no, rather; on the contrary

    adverb, opening the correction · also used · classical · Sen. Ep. 47.1: ‘servī sunt.’ immō hominēs.; Cic. Off. 3.90: Immō vērō obsecrābit patrem; de Vaan 300, s.v. immō; Traupman p. 111: immō, well

    The “actually” of a correction. Never an answer on its own, unlike minimē: it always brings the corrected statement (Lewis & Short).

  • rēapse — in fact, in reality

    adverb · also used · classical · Cic. Rep. 1.2: rēapse, nōn ōrātiōne (Lewis & Short); Plaut. Truc. 4.3.41 (Lewis & Short)

    An old word, not found after Cicero (Lewis & Short).

  • rē ipsā — in fact, in the event

    adverbial ablative · also used · classical · Cic. Rosc. Am. 123: tametsī verbō nōn audeat, tamen rē ipsā (Lewis & Short)

  • āctuāliter — actively

    avoid · late Latin · Myth. Vat. 3 (Lewis & Short, s.v. actualis)

    Late Latin for “actively”, from āctuālis, “active, practical” (Macr.). It never means “in fact”.

Examples

  • et quidem multō parcius scrīpsī quam rē vērā furere eōs invēnī

    and indeed I wrote much more mildly than the frenzy I actually found them inLentulus in Cic. Fam. 12.14.3

  • ‘servī sunt.’ immō hominēs. ‘servī sunt.’ immō contubernālēs.

    “They’re slaves.” No, actually, they’re people. “They’re slaves.” No, actually, they share our roof.Sen. Ep. 47.1

  • silēbitne fīlius? Immō vērō obsecrābit patrem, nē id faciat

    will the son say nothing? Actually, no: he will beg his father not to do itCic. Off. 3.90

See also truly, fact.
